parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a national document/visa regime — X markers barred, mismatched documents trigger refusal and possible fraud-based lifetime ineligibility, passports confiscated stranding travellers, foreign governments issuing trans travel advisories — with a state facility statute covering airports, courthouses, parks and schools, enforced by order-to-leave and criminal trespass (one documented arrest, 24 hours in a men's ward). Adults also face care barriers and conscience refusal; immigration custody documents beatings, forced labour and sexual abuse of trans men; trans-women killings run 3.7/100k. Mitigating: no identity criminalisation, national hate-crime and employment protections, courts enjoining orders, legal aid, private premises open, most sibling states unbanned. Worst feature is tier-1 universal exposure with partial, uneven remedy.

entry_documents.exposure: National Feb-2025 rule bars X markers and markers differing from assigned sex; consular cable instructs refusal where documents cast doubt on sex, with fraud-based lifetime ineligibility considered; travellers report passports confiscated or blocked, stranded abroad. Documented.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry; refusal requires four fraud elements, never automatic, with limited waiver; unresolved litigation and a legal-aid FAQ. Partial.
entry_documents.interaction: Border refusal or detention can move a visitor into immigration custody, where trans men document forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: State facility law converts presence after an order to leave into criminal trespass (up to 60 days); one trans woman arrested and held 24 hours in a men's ward. Immigration-custody abuse of trans men documented. National corrections conversion-therapy policy reaches anyone entering federal custody.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Only one arrest documented; that case dismissed; entry requires willful refusal to depart, not automatic arrest; courts functioning.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A border document discrepancy plus a facility refusal can chain into arrest, custody placement by birth sex and hostile federal facilities.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State statute bans identity-congruent restroom/changing use in all government-owned or leased buildings — offices, courthouses, parks, beaches, airports, schools — with gender labelling, authority figure empowered to order departure and trespass charge; applies to visitors and residents alike. Tier-1 universal exposure.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Private businesses expressly outside scope; no later prosecution documented; the single case dismissed on standing; 29 sibling states plus capital district have no mapped ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Airport application is not documented in practice, so exposure at ports of entry is plausible but unconfirmed; national facility orders reinforce state bans.

care_services.exposure: State bars care for minors, restricts adults (physicians-only, 24-hour wait, insurance bar) and since May 2023 permits practitioner refusal on conscience grounds; federal orders and funding actions target trans care; crisis-lifeline LGBTQ line shut down.
care_services.protection: A federal judge permanently blocked minor and adult care bans (June 2024, appeal status unresolved); preliminary injunctions show courts working for trans people; emergency care not documented as denied.
care_services.interaction: A travelling parent seeking care for a trans minor faces state bans plus federal scrutiny; conscience refusal can strand a visitor mid-treatment.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal executive orders redefine sex binary, ban 'gender ideology' materials, direct investigation of schools and prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition; counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups for identification and neutralisation; 'radical gender ideology' listed among extremist animating viewpoints.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Reward criteria expressly exclude the phrase as a trigger; strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; orders partly enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Heightened official framing raises the odds any stop, border check or facility refusal escalates, and is cited in foreign travel advisories.

minors_guardians.exposure: Facility bans reach K-12 and all schools public and private; state care ban for minors (partly blocked); 2023 custody-modification law permits changing custody where a child received or may receive gender-affirming care, with protests involving detained trans children documented.
minors_guardians.protection: Federal permanent injunction against minor-care provisions (appellate status unresolved); conversion-therapy city bans struck down nationally; custody law largely resident-facing.
minors_guardians.interaction: A visiting family with a trans minor risks school exclusion, care denial and — in a worst case — custody framing if care is sought.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 3.7 trans women murdered per 100k per year, state labelled 'Do Not Travel'; national risk assessment flags 4 states similarly; national hate-crime bias statistics persistent. Only one arrest pattern of police targeting documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; analysis finds flat correlation between hostile law and killing rates (no organised campaign); employment and many local public-accommodation protections operate.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State hate-crime law omits gender identity, so state-level recourse is thinner than federal; background homicide rate not supplied, so magnitude is uncertain.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Facility statute never substantively tested; driver's licence fraud rule and birth-certificate closure unlitigated; airport application undocumented; travel advisories' current status unresolved; oversight uneven — 37 states lacked gender-identity bias statutes as of 2019.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning courts have enjoined multiple federal orders, permanently blocked care bans and dismissed the sole prosecution; ACLU litigation, legal-aid FAQs, state human-relations commission enforcement operate.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Partial remedy plus unresolved questions means outcomes depend on forum and moment, but exposure is documented regardless of the open questions.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra bars and expels trans visitors categorically through a register with no remedy. Here entry is not categorically barred: consistent-document trans travellers may enter and much of the country imposes no facility ban. But the document-discrepancy refusal rule plus criminal facility exclusion at airports and government buildings is comparably broad in daily reach, so the case sits above this anchor.

Vesskar shows routine checkpoint exposure, a public-order statute on presentation, lengthy verification detentions, scarce legal aid and inconsistent enforcement. Very close: this dossier adds a criminal facility statute with a real arrest and worse immigration-custody abuse, but also national hate-crime/employment protections and courts that repeatedly enjoin hostile orders. Rough parity, slightly lower on severity, higher on remedy.

Kestrel Isles offers only administrative secondary screening, refusal and return with an appeal desk. This dossier is clearly worse: potential permanent fraud ineligibility, confiscated passports stranding travellers, criminal trespass exposure in public buildings, documented custody abuse, and foreign 'Do Not Travel' advisories. Must rate materially below 0.55.

Meridia has trained border officers, respectful inspection, brief detention ending in release, compensation and counsel. Almost none of that is documented here: screening is instructed to refuse on sex doubt, facilities are legally exclusionary, custody is documented as abusive. Clearly below 0.75 by a wide margin.

parsed.synthesis: Two universal-exposure layers interact: the border document/visa regime (mismatch → refusal, possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, confiscated passports) and the state facility statute (airports, courthouses, parks, schools → order to leave → criminal trespass, one arrest with men's-ward detention). An outed visitor can move from document scrutiny to refusal into immigration custody, where trans detainees document beatings, forced labour and sexual abuse — state-tolerated tier-2 harm. Care access narrows through conscience refusal and unresolved bans, biting hardest on a travelling minor. Violence is elevated (3.7/100k trans women, 'Do Not Travel') but untrended to hostile law, so background-elevated rather than a campaign. Offsetting: no identity criminalisation, federal hate-crime and employment protections, functioning courts enjoining orders, dismissed sole prosecution, private premises open, most sibling states unbanned. Net: documented tier-1 exposure with partial, uneven remedy — Elevated Risk.
